_meta.label: AI-generated data file: built by code written with an AI assistant (Claude Code); no language model ran to build it. Counts of the gpt-oss:20b card sentences, the code gates and the review verdicts, computed by code. Team output, not a NASA conclusion.

description: Measured counts for the model-written card sentences (gpt-oss:20b) and their checks, reproduced by ai/apply_review.py from ai/review/review_sheet.csv and the gate results of ai/apply_cards.py. Rates are measured before removal and carry their n. Rows read by an AI session are never counted as read by a person. Reviewed by hackathon team members or a second AI session, not by NASA or a combustion expert.
rejected_by_gate_note: rejected_by_gate counts every failing gate of a first-pass sentence (a sentence can fail several); rejected_first_gate counts each rejected sentence once. 'key_point' is the writer rule that the first cited unit is a quotable sentence.

sentences.sentence: The investigation aimed to bridge the gap between normal gravity tests and microgravity flammability, and to assess inert gaseous extinguishing agents on various materials. (PSI-26 record: objective)
sentences.reason: Stronger than the record, and wrong in number. The first objective in the record is to 'Begin to bridge the gap between the normal gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test#1 method, ground-based microgravity tests, and actual material flammability in microgravity' (OBJ-2). The sentence drops 'Begin to' and names two of the three things, so the aim reads as bridging the gap outright. The second objective is to 'Assess the effectiveness of an inert, gaseous extinguishing agent (similar to that used on ISS)' (OBJ-5): one agent. The sentence says 'agents', as if several were assessed. Removed; the slot shows the quoted NASA sentence.

sentences.sentence: The record hypothesizes that differences between fire behavior in normal and reduced gravity make terrestrial fire standards risky for spacecraft safety. (PSI-99 record: hypothesis)
sentences.reason: Subject changed and the stated reason dropped. The record says 'the use of terrestrial fires and fire standards to design spacecraft fire safety systems presents an inherent risk to the vehicle because of the significant level of uncertainty' (HYP-1). The sentence says the differences 'make terrestrial fire standards risky for spacecraft safety': the risk moves from using terrestrial fires and standards for design to the standards themselves, 'terrestrial fires' and 'to the vehicle' are gone, and 'because of the significant level of uncertainty' is left out, so it reads as a verdict on the standards. Removed; the slot shows the quoted NASA sentence.

sentences.sentence: The record states that space benefits include potential to improve spacecraft fire-safety modeling by resolving cool-flame/extinction behavior in microgravity and defining operating envelopes. (PSI-117 record: researchImpacts)
sentences.reason: Two separate items of the record are joined into one claim, and words are lost. The record says 'Potential to improve spacecraft fire-safety modeling by resolving cool-flame/extinction behavior in microgravity; leverages FLEX to define safer operating envelopes/materials' (IMP-1). In the sentence the potential is to improve the modeling 'by resolving cool-flame/extinction behavior in microgravity and defining operating envelopes': defining envelopes becomes a way of improving the modeling, which the record does not say, and 'leverages FLEX', 'safer' and 'materials' are dropped. Removed; the slot shows the quoted NASA sentence.

sentences.sentence: The record hypothesizes that testing aboard the ISS can demonstrate the first-time improvement in understanding cool flame kinetics. (PSI-159 record: hypothesis)
sentences.reason: A clipped sentence completed with the model's own words. The record says testing aboard the ISS 'can demonstrate the following for the first time, contributing to an improved understanding of cool flame kinetics' (HYP-1), and 'the following' is the list of flames in HYP-2 to HYP-6 (for example 'Steady-state cool diffusion flames on spherical porous burners'). The sentence says testing 'can demonstrate the first-time improvement in understanding cool flame kinetics': what would be shown for the first time is the listed flames, not an improvement in understanding, which the record only says they contribute to. Removed; the slot shows the quoted NASA sentence.

removed_before_review.rule: sentences that passed every code gate and were removed by the pm session's reviewed removals (ai/review/pm_prereview.json) before the review; each slot shows the quoted NASA sentence it cited. Counted apart from the review: not part of removed_by_review, verdicts or the support rate, and never a reason to set reviewed_by.

support_rate_rule: supported / reviewed model sentences, before removal; null while n is 0
